we used reverse-phase protein microarrays to measure the levels of six NER proteins in cultured lymphocytes from controls and SCCHN cases.
low expression of XPC, XPD, XPF, and XPA is associated with increased risk of SCChN, and that XPF is the most critical protein in NER.

the expression of nucleotide excise repair (NER) proteins in human lymphocytes is significantly lower in patients with newly diagnosed squamous cell carcinoma of the head and Neck (SCCHN) compared with controls.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of NER proteins in lymphocytes as a marker of susceptibility to SCCHN.
the role of DNA repair in cancer susceptibility.
the development of a reverse-phase microarray assay to measure the levels of nucleotide-excision repair proteins in cultured human lymphocytes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NER protein levels are significantly associated with risk of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, particularly for XPF, but the study was too small to draw a definite conclusion.
low expression of XPC, XPF, XPG, XPD, ERCC1, and XPA in lymphocytes may increase risk of SCCHNs.
XPF expression in lymphocytes is associated with risk for head and neck cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
XPF is a key factor in NER.
XPF may play a critical role in DNA repair and the reverse-protein assay may be a powerful tool in measuring the protein markers of susceptibility for cancer.
low levels of NER protein expression in lymphocytes may be an early biomarker for SCCHN susceptibility.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression levels of NER proteins may be used as a marker for the risk of SCCHNs, particularly for XPC, XPA, and XPF.
the expression levels of the proteins involved in NER are associated with the risk of SCCHNs.
the expression levels of NER proteins in lymphocytes are associated with susceptibility to SCCHN.
